AccountRecord.description:
An account as a draft saves it (S12.15): its type is chosen when it is made; its
settings are its owner's (S10.3).
AccountRecord.title: AccountRecord

AnchorRecord.description: A balance typed from the institution's site (S1.11.2), as its dialog's draft saves it.
AnchorRecord.title: AnchorRecord

AssumptionsRecord.description:
A user's own assumptions as a draft saves them (S6.3): every figure, checked together;
made when they first change the shipped ones, deleted to go back to them.
AssumptionsRecord.title: AssumptionsRecord

BookAccountRecord.description:
An account a tax book counts or leaves out beyond what its filers' own say (S8.14.2):
one the caller can see added (a custodial account in a child's name), or one of the
filers' own left out. Deleted, the book counts it as its filers' accounts say.
BookAccountRecord.title: BookAccountRecord

BookRecord.description:
A tax book as a draft saves it (S8.14): its year and filers are chosen when it is made;
how it reads bitcoin network fees may change (S8.19).
BookRecord.title: BookRecord

BudgetRecord.description:
A budget as a draft saves it (S7.1): its method chosen when it is made; its accounts
its owner's choice; its roles a card's paying account or where reserves' money moves from,
chosen (none: as the history says).
BudgetRecord.title: BudgetRecord

CardLine.description: A card's payment line in an envelope budget (S7.13.2).
CardLine.title: CardLine

CategoryRecord.description:
A category as a draft saves it (S2.5): made with its name, kind and parent; afterwards
only how long receipts in it are kept, an admin's, since it decides what file pruning may
remove (S14.10.1.1).
CategoryRecord.title: CategoryRecord

Clash.description:
Someone already here by a name (S10.10.3): who, whether the caller sees them, and who
added them, to use them or ask them to be shared.
Clash.title: Clash

ColourRecord.description: The colour of a linked household's window, for its chooser (S12.10.3.2).
ColourRecord.title: ColourRecord

CompareView.description: The active budget and one scenario side by side (S7.12.3).
CompareView.title: CompareView

ConnectionRecord.description:
A Connection as a draft saves it (S18.6): its driver chosen when it is made; its name
and settings its owner's to change, the institution's address only with the password
again. Its sign-in is never here: it is sealed apart (S18.7).
ConnectionRecord.title: ConnectionRecord

ConnectorInfo.description: What any user needs to start a Connection: whether a connector is paired, and its keys.
ConnectorInfo.title: ConnectorInfo

ContributionRecord.description:
A contribution's tag as a draft saves it (S1.8.2): who made a deposit into the 529 and
whether it is a five-year election. Made for a deposit already there (an imported one), or
with the deposit it records, from a bank account with both halves.
ContributionRecord.title: ContributionRecord

CorporateActionRecord.description: A corporate action as its dialog's draft saves it (S2.4).
CorporateActionRecord.title: CorporateActionRecord

CountedRecord.description:
A receiver's Count in my totals on an account shared with them (S10.7), off until they
tick it; their own, as its record of the save.
CountedRecord.title: CountedRecord

Credential.description: A credential sealed in the browser to the connector's sealing key: the box as it is.
Credential.title: Credential

Deleted.description:
Every DELETE's answer (S13.8.1): what went, and what it belonged to as it now stands,
or null for a record that belonged to nothing.
Deleted.title: Deleted

DependentRecord.description: A dependent of a book (S8.14.5), with the accounts in their name it counts.
DependentRecord.title: DependentRecord

DocumentRecord.description: A tax document of a book (S8.16), received or filed, with its file.
DocumentRecord.title: DocumentRecord

DonationRecord.description:
A donation as a draft saves it (S7.9.2): recorded whole; afterwards only what changes
after the fact does, the acknowledgement arriving (its file among `receiptIds`), a grant
paid, the organisation, notes.
DonationRecord.title: DonationRecord

EducationPlanRecord.description: A 529's plan as a draft saves it (S1.8.1): made with the account or on its Settings.
EducationPlanRecord.title: EducationPlanRecord

Equity.description: What the loan is secured by, and the borrower's stake in it (S1.9.5).
Equity.title: Equity

ExpenseRecord.description: A qualified expense as a draft saves it (S1.8.3), in its 529's account.
ExpenseRecord.title: ExpenseRecord

FigureRecord.description:
An admin's correction of one shipped tax-table figure for a year (S16.11), as the tax
tables' draft saves it; the shipped value again deletes it.
FigureRecord.title: FigureRecord

FilingRecord.description:
A filing as a draft saves it: its estimated payments are records of their own
(`EstPy`), so each keeps its matched transaction.
FilingRecord.title: FilingRecord

GiftRecord.description:
A gift as a draft saves it (S7.8), with its people as a set and the receipts kept with
it (`receiptIds`).
GiftRecord.title: GiftRecord

GivingPlanRecord.description: A year's giving plan as a draft saves it (S7.9.1).
GivingPlanRecord.title: GivingPlanRecord

Gone.description:
What a DELETE took away (S13.8.1): its id (for a pair, its two keys joined by a slash),
when, and the version it had.
Gone.title: Gone

GroupRecord.description: A group as an admin's draft saves it (S10.2): the built-in admins keep their name.
GroupRecord.title: GroupRecord

HeldInOut.description: An account reserves are held in, and what is to move there (S7.10.4).
HeldInOut.title: HeldInOut

InBudget.description: A budget counting a transaction, what it counts as there, and its leave-out (S7.3.5).
InBudget.title: InBudget

Incoming.description:
A share crossing the link, either way, as an admin here sees it (S11.3, S11.7): its
kind, owner, date and who it names, never its name or figures.
Incoming.title: Incoming

ItemRecord.description:
An item as a draft saves it, with its sale (S1.10.5) and the photos and documents kept
with it (`receiptIds`, a set of uploaded receipts). Its valuations and improvements are
records of their own.
ItemRecord.title: ItemRecord

LeftOut.description: An account the budget doesn't count that often receives transfers from its accounts.
LeftOut.title: LeftOut

LineIn.description:
A plan line as a draft saves it: the line holds from `fromMonth` on, earlier months
keeping the plan they had (S7.1.2).
LineIn.title: LineIn

LineOut.description: A plan line as it is stored (S7.1.2), which a dialog's draft starts from (S12.15.1).
LineOut.title: LineOut

LoanRecord.description:
A loan's terms as a draft saves them: set when the loan is made, corrected later (an
ARM's resets, a recast).
LoanRecord.title: LoanRecord

MoveOut.description: An amount put from one category to another for the month (S7.11).
MoveOut.title: MoveOut

MoveRecord.description:
A move as a draft makes it (S7.11): made, or deleted to undo it. With a transaction,
landed money given to a reserve held where it landed, or to no category: kept as the
account's own (S7.10.5); its month is the transaction's.
MoveRecord.title: MoveRecord

MovedRow.description:
A transfer between one of the budget's accounts and one it doesn't count, with no
category: it counts nowhere until sorted (S7.3.2).
MovedRow.title: MovedRow

OccasionRecord.description:
An occasion of a gift plan (S7.7.1): a holiday by its key, or an anniversary or other
occasion on a month and day, with the year it began when known.
OccasionRecord.title: OccasionRecord

OrganisationRecord.description: An organisation as a draft saves it (S7.9.5).
OrganisationRecord.title: OrganisationRecord

PaymentRecord.description: An estimated tax payment of a filing (S8.15), matched to its transaction.
PaymentRecord.title: PaymentRecord

PaymentView.description: A payment as shown; its own model, so the contract has one schema each way.
PaymentView.title: PaymentView

PayoffRecord.description: A saved overpayment plan as a draft saves it (S1.9.6).
PayoffRecord.title: PayoffRecord

PersonOut.description: A gift plan the caller sees, with its person.
PersonOut.title: PersonOut

PersonRecord.description:
A person as a draft saves them. `differentPerson`, on a new one, says a name already
here is someone else, told apart by birth year (S10.10.3).
PersonRecord.title: PersonRecord

PlanRecord.description:
A gift plan as a draft saves it: its occasions are records of their own (`Occsn`), so
each keeps its id, and the gifts planned for it stay with it (CR3-43).
PlanRecord.title: PlanRecord

PlanView.description: The inputs as saved; its own models, so the contract has one schema for each direction.
PlanView.title: PlanView

PortfolioRecord.description: A portfolio as a draft saves it (S5.1): its accounts are its owner's choice.
PortfolioRecord.title: PortfolioRecord

Problem.description: A refusal (S13.8.3): its code is one of those listed, and stable.

ProjectionRecord.description:
A projection as a draft saves it (S6.6): its goal chosen when it is made. An active
one's new inputs become its baseline only when `rebaseline` asks it (S6.7.4); it is an
instruction, never kept.
ProjectionRecord.title: ProjectionRecord

Proposal.description: A plan line estimated from history (S7.1.5).
Proposal.title: Proposal

ReceiptLinkRecord.description:
What a receipt is attached to, as a draft makes or takes it away (S9.3): a record of
its own, never changed. `itemId` names a record of the kind's table.
ReceiptLinkRecord.title: ReceiptLinkRecord

ReceiptRecord.description:
A receipt as a draft saves it (S9.8): what was read from it, or typed, and whether it is
kept for ever. It is made by uploading its file; what it is attached to are pairs of their
own (S13.8.6).
ReceiptRecord.title: ReceiptRecord

ReconciliationRecord.description:
Ticking off against a statement (S1.11.6), as its dialog's draft saves it: made with the
statement's closing date and balance; `finished` once the ticked transactions leave no
difference, which marks them reconciled. A finished one stays; an unfinished one may go.
ReconciliationRecord.title: ReconciliationRecord

RecoveryCodes.description: Shown once: only their hashes are kept.
RecoveryCodes.title: RecoveryCodes

Relation.description: Someone the user is related to (S10.10.6): stored, or worked out from those.
Relation.title: Relation

RelationshipRecord.description:
A relationship as a draft saves it (S10.10.4): a marriage changed in any way is
confirmed again by the other.
RelationshipRecord.title: RelationshipRecord

Restarting.description:
A re-encryption or a rotation scheduled, and the server restarting for it (S15.7.2):
the browser waits for the locked screen, where the phrase starts it.
Restarting.title: Restarting

ReviewView.description:
The month's review (S7.14): its loose ends, each with its action, and whether it was
reviewed and has changed since.
ReviewView.title: ReviewView

RoleOut.description: Where an account's money comes from (S7.1.6), worked out unless chosen.
RoleOut.title: RoleOut

RuleRecord.description:
A rule as a draft saves it (S2.7): a new one goes last in the list, and one moved goes
to its `position` (from 0), the others closing up around it; the tags it sets are its
owner's.
RuleRecord.title: RuleRecord

Saved.description: A record the save touched: its new version and the record as read, or what went.
Saved.title: Saved

SettingRecord.description:
A setting as a section's draft saves it (S16): its key, and a value its definition
checks; a password's value is written and never read back, null removing it.
SettingRecord.title: SettingRecord

SettingRef.description: A saved setting's record: its id and version (S13.8.6).
SettingRef.title: SettingRef

ShareRecord.description:
A grant as the share dialog's draft saves it (S10.4): an item shared with one user or
one group, at Read or Write; with a linked server's person, at Read, with Include receipts
their images and text cross too (S11.5.1). It stays with its item and its grantee.
ShareRecord.title: ShareRecord

SignupOpen.description: Whether the sign-in screen offers Sign up, and to which email domains.
SignupOpen.title: SignupOpen

SourceRecord.description:
A price source as a draft saves it (S4.2): added by name; on or off, its place for
each class it serves, and its key, a secret written and never read back (S14.4).

apiKey.description: the source's key, written, never read back
apiKey.title: Apikey

SourceRecord.title: SourceRecord

SplitRecord.description: A part of a transaction's amount with its own category (S2.6), as a draft saves it.
SplitRecord.title: SplitRecord

Spouse.description: Who the user is married to today, when they are a user here (S10.10.4.3).
Spouse.title: Spouse

StrategyRecord.description:
A strategy as a draft saves it (S3.5): grouped from legs held in its account, by hand or
as proposed, or a proposal turned down (`dismissed`, kept so it isn't proposed again); then
its name, cash-secured tick and margin. Undone by deleting it, its legs standing on their
own again.
StrategyRecord.title: StrategyRecord

Suggested.description: A field read from the receipt, with how sure the reader was (0–100).
Suggested.title: Suggested

TagRecord.description: A tag as a draft saves it: its name, lower case, once its owner's.
TagRecord.title: TagRecord

TokenRecord.description:
A token as a draft makes it (S10.9): made once, its secret in the save's answer alone;
never changed; revoked by deleting it.
TokenRecord.title: TokenRecord

TransferIn.description: A transfer in from the budget's accounts this month: the reserves' unless kept.
TransferIn.title: TransferIn

TwoStepNeeded.description: The password was right and two-step sign-in is on: the code comes next (S10.1.6).
TwoStepNeeded.title: TwoStepNeeded

TwoStepSetup.description: What an authenticator app needs: the QR code, or the key typed by hand.
TwoStepSetup.title: TwoStepSetup

TxfLeftOut.description: The sales the TXF file leaves out, by why, to be entered from the CSV (S8.2).
TxfLeftOut.title: TxfLeftOut

TxnRecord.description:
A transaction as a draft saves it: its splits are records of their own (`Split`), so
each keeps its id, and with it what pays it back (S2.9). `symbol` names a new trade's
instrument; `leftOutOf` lists the budgets it is left out of (S7.3.5).
TxnRecord.title: TxnRecord

TypedPriceRecord.description:
A price from a statement, or typed, with its date (S4.3), as its dialog's draft saves
it: its typer's alone, valuing their own accounts and never another user's (S4.10), one a
day.
TypedPriceRecord.title: TypedPriceRecord

UserRecord.description:
A user as a draft saves them: an admin's (S10.1), invited when made, their email
changed only while the invitation is pending; and the user's own Profile (S12.2.16),
theirs alone, their sex and birthday their person's (S10.10.1).
UserRecord.title: UserRecord

moolakata__ui__budgets__PlanOut.description: The lines in force in a month, each as stored; a line of 0 is none.
moolakata__ui__budgets__PlanOut.title: PlanOut

moolakata__ui__links__CopyOut.description: The link's copy (S11.7): its access key, size, and whether it is unlocked.
moolakata__ui__links__CopyOut.title: CopyOut

moolakata__ui__loans__SplitOut.description:
How the schedule splits a payment (S1.9.3), and the category each part is recorded in;
the overpayment is principal beyond the schedule's, part of `principal`.
moolakata__ui__loans__SplitOut.title: SplitOut

moolakata__ui__receipts__LinkOut.description:
A transaction it supports, the account it is kept on (a statement), or what else it is
kept with: an item, a qualified expense, a gift, a donation, a tax document. `id` and
`version` are the link's own (`ReceiptLink`); a tax document's file has none.
moolakata__ui__receipts__LinkOut.title: LinkOut

moolakata__ui__settings__SecretSet.description: A stored secret as the UI shows it: set, when and by whom.
moolakata__ui__settings__SecretSet.title: SecretSet

info.description: The browser app's API, /ui/api (requirements S13.8). It is served with the app and carries no version of its own.
info.title: MoolaKata

get.description: The beneficiary's education projection: the active one, else the first made.

post.description:
An education projection for the beneficiary, built on their 529s the caller can see,
starting from the shipped public-college average and this year's contributions.

Location.description: Where what was made is read: its own path, or the list or record that holds it. Left out when nothing reads it.

get.description:
Bank transactions of the last 90 days that look like this loan's payment (within 2% of
it, not yet a transfer, and not filed under some other category, as rent is), to link
with one click.

post.description:
A plan's overpayments against the schedule: the new payoff date, months and interest
saved, a recast after its lump sums, and the same money invested instead.

Marks the plan being followed, tracked from today, or stops following it; the one
followed before stops. An action: it changes every plan of the loan.

get.description:
How the schedule would split a payment of this amount on this day: the parts a payment's
draft records, a split of its transaction (S1.9.3).

post.description: An option's end: it expired, was assigned, or was exercised (S3.4, S3.6).

schema.title: Response Settle Ui Api Accounts  Account Id  Options  Instrument Id  Settle Post

Location.description: Where what was made is read: its own path, or the list or record that holds it. Left out when nothing reads it.

post.description:
A statement to keep on its account as it is: its period and institution are read where
they can be, for the person to check.
Read the wallet from the explorer or node now (S1.6.2).

get.description: How many entries arrived after one the page shows: the +N new pill (S12.1.3).

Open alerts first, newest first, then those resolved in the last 90 days; an alert
the caller dismissed is left out.

post.description: Opening the screen marks the caller's alerts as seen, which clears the badge.
Dismissed for the caller alone; it stays open for anyone else it is for.

schema.title: Response Badges Ui Api Badges Get

get.description: Compare models: each one's median path and its figures for 2030, 2035 and 2045.

The caller's accounts outside these that received two or more transfers from them in
the last year, to name when a budget is made or edited (S7.3.2). Loans are counted by
their payments, so they're never named.
One budget, as its list shows it: where a new one's Location leads (S13.8.4).

Two budgets side by side, per category: what is available and spent, for the month or
the year to it (S7.12.3).

post.description:
Copy as scenario (S7.12.4): the same accounts and plan from this month, in the method
chosen, with this month's moves when asked. The copy is the caller's; the budget they
follow doesn't change.

Location.description: Where what was made is read: its own path, or the list or record that holds it. Left out when nothing reads it.

get.description: A plan from the last 3, 6 or 12 complete months (S7.1.5): nothing is saved.

The plan as it holds in a month, line by line as stored: what the plan dialog edits
(S7.1.2), never the month's figures, which add carried amounts and moves to it.
Found in the last 15 months of the budget's accounts each time it is asked.

post.description: Refresh: the budget's months worked out again at once (S7.3.10).

get.description:
What the budget's accounts await, oldest first, each with the deposits that may pay it
back among the caller's own accounts and those they can change.

The month before this one unless another is asked: what was overspent, what is to move,
what is left in To Budget, and what waits to be sorted (S7.14).

post.description:
Mark reviewed (S7.14): who and when, and the month's figures then, so a later change is
flagged until it is reviewed again. Months are never locked.

get.description:
Where the money is (S7.10.4): each account reserves are held in, what is to move there
or back, the money landed there waiting to be given, and each card's payments.
Net worth over time, with its composition by account group (S5.3).

The live stream (S12.6): what changed, never data. It ends after a few minutes and
the browser reconnects; it never extends the session.

Recent spending, to link a gift's cost to its transaction: the last 90 days, in the
accounts the caller writes to, since linking may recategorise it.

delete.description:
An upload its dialog no longer needs (closed, or cancelled), let go at once rather than
when it expires. Held in memory, it has no version; one already gone answers the same.

post.description:
The ending value becomes a value anchor on the last day; the positions a holdings check
(or, for an account kept by snapshots, its holdings that day); the cash lines kept become
transactions; and the PDF is kept on the account. Trades are never added here.

Kept on the account as a receipt named by its period, its period recorded so it counts
as the statement expected (S1.11.7), its lines never added.

Nothing is saved until the person has checked it: the rows they keep become
transactions (what is already there is matched, not added twice), the balances become the
account's anchors, the file is kept as a receipt on the account, and the layout is learned
for the next statement from this institution. A statement of several accounts is saved
once each part is saved or left out.

get.description:
Items a loan can be secured by: unsold property, vehicles and other assets the caller
can see (S1.9.5).
The households that share something with you (S12.10.1); none share nothing.
One document of an item shared with you, as its source answered it for you.
The receipts that crossed with items shared with you (S11.5.1).

A receipt, streamed through decryption into the answer: its plain bytes never touch the
disk, and its hash, signed at the source, is checked as it goes (S11.9.6.4, S11.9.6.5).
What this household shares with you, each with its row (S12.10.3.4).

post.description: Lock now (S11.9.4.3): anyone the copy shares with.
The 12 words (S11.9.3.1): checked here, held in memory; nothing reaches the browser.

Each open contract to its new root, strike and deliverable, from the OCC's memo; its
lots carry over in every account the caller may change, nothing sold (S3.10.2).

get.description:
The caller's open contracts, by underlying, that an adjustment from the OCC's memo can
change: in the accounts they may change.

post.description: The answer is the same whether or not the user exists (S10.1.5).

get.description: The caller's gift plans and those shared with them, with their people.
One gift plan the caller sees, with its person: what the plan's dialog starts from.
The household's people the caller can see, with how each is related to them.

The person a new one by this name would be, when there is one: what a dialog shows when
its save is refused as `person-exists`.

schema.title: Response Person Clash Ui Api Persons Clash Get

get.description: One person the caller can see: where a new one's Location leads (S13.8.4).

post.description: Ask whoever added a private person, and the admins, to share them (S10.10.3).
A remote user is this person (S10.10.1): confirmed by someone who may change it.

get.description: Everyone the person is related to as of a day, stored and worked out (S10.10.5).
What the portfolio's visible accounts hold, added up by instrument.
Time-weighted returns per period, per account and for the portfolio (S5.2.3).

Value over time with contributions apart from growth, against the benchmark, and the
period's time- and money-weighted returns (S5.2.1, S5.2.3).

Realized gains grouped by year, month, account, instrument or term (S3.9), and
unrealized gains now, by account or instrument.

Each option trade (S3.9): from the first contract opened to the last one closed, with the
premium in and out, its P/L and its return on the capital at risk. A long option risks its
premium; a short one the strike on every contract's shares, cash for a put and the shares
for a call.

Open strategies first, then those closed; the proposals for the accounts the caller
may change.

post.description: Refresh prices: the daily task, now (S4.4), followed as a job (S13.8.7).

The credential sealed in the browser (S18.7.1): kept as it is until the connector
collects it on its next report. A secret, replaced outright: an action, with no version
(S13.8.6). The
password again (S13.7.2), and only once an admin confirmed the pairing (S18.4.3).

Ends every session; this browser gets a fresh one (S13.7.1). A wrong current password
counts toward the sign-in's lockout (S13.7.5.1).
Turning two-step on starts here; it is on once a code from the app is confirmed.
Two-step sign-in off, with the password again (S13.7.2): an action on the user.
New codes replace every old one.

At most one active per subject: the one it replaces goes back to being a scenario.
Its median path and 10th–90th band as of today become its baseline (S6.7.2).

The same answer whatever the account's state, and a wrong password counted as a
sign-in's (S10.1.7).

get.description:
Newest first. *inbox*: the caller's receipts attached to nothing yet. The search looks
in what was read from each receipt (S9.8.5) as well as its fields.

post.description:
One file per request; a batch is many requests. The same file again gives back the
receipt it made (200).

Location.description: Where what was made is read: its own path, or the list or record that holds it. Left out when nothing reads it.

get.description:
Streamed through decryption, never written out as plaintext. Served inline in a
sandbox, with its checked type, so a PDF can't run script in the app (S9.4).

post.description: Read it again (S9.8.6): only empty or suggested fields are replaced.

get.description: The stored relationships of a person (the caller's own by default).

post.description:
A spouse confirms the marriage from their own Profile, or an admin for a person who
isn't a user (S10.10.4); once both have, it counts for wash sales and tax books.

The rules over the uncategorised transactions in the accounts the user can change; how
many changed is recorded, never which (S2.7.4).
A dialog's draft, saved all or nothing (S13.8.11).

delete.description: Signing out ends every session of the user at once (S13.7.1).

post.description: The password again, counted toward the sign-in's lockout (S13.7.2, S13.7.5.1).

The second step: a code from the app, or one of the recovery codes (S10.1.6). One code
at a time for each sign-in, slowed before it is checked, and five wrong ones end the
sign-in, so the password is needed again (S10.1.6.3).

*Copies kept* (S16.12): the days of backups kept. Fewer than the backups there are
deletes some at the next backup, so that takes the password again and the recovery
phrase, as Remove does (S16.13); a wrong phrase counts toward the sign-in's lockout.
Back up now: the daily task, at once, followed as a job (S13.8.7).

An admin confirms the Electrum server's certificate, as Test showed it: it is then the
one trusted, and any other refused (S1.6.2.4).
Ask the saved explorer or node for the chain's height, and say what failed.

Accept (S18.2.4.4): the address the connector now reports from is its own. The
password again (S13.7.2).

Confirm (S18.4.3): the admin compared the fingerprint both sides show. Until then the
connector gets no sealed credential and posts no file. The password again (S13.7.2).

Pair (S18.4.1): a one-time code, valid 24 hours, shown once; the password again if given
over 10 minutes ago (S13.7.2).

Location.description: Where what was made is read: its own path, or the list or record that holds it. Left out when nothing reads it.

post.description:
Unpair (S18.4.4): the connector's key is refused from then on, every Connection stops
and every account's sync turns off.
Send a test email to the admin now, through the saved settings, and say what failed.

get.description:
The emails written to the mail folder while SMTP was not set up (S16.2), newest
first: who they are for and what they say, for an admin to pass a link on.

One written email, links and all: the password again (S13.7.2), since a link in it is
a token that signs someone in or resets a password.

Key storage (S16.13): the master key's state, its previous keys, and the last
re-encryption; the copies come from their own route.

Every copy on this host, with how it opens; snapshots and the host's backups are not
here (S15.7).

delete.description:
Remove one copy (S15.8 step 4): the password again and the recovery phrase, so an
admin's session alone deletes no backup (S13.7.2, S16.13). A wrong phrase counts toward
the sign-in's lockout.
Drop a previous master key from the keyring's list once nothing needs it (S15.7.1).

post.description:
Re-encrypt now (S15.7.2): scheduled with each copy's choice, and the server restarts at
once; the unlock that follows runs it before the server serves, with the phrase given
there. It never runs while the server serves, and once scheduled it is not withdrawn
(CR3-61). The password again (S13.7.2).

Rotate (S15.7.1): a new master key and phrase, and with them a new data key. The
password again and the current phrase, or a break-glass code from the host, so an
admin's session alone can't change the phrase the household holds; a wrong one counts
toward the sign-in's lockout. Three of the new phrase's words typed back; then the
keyring is wrapped under it and the server restarts, and the unlock with the new phrase
re-encrypts (S15.7.2).

A rotation's new phrase (S15.7.1), made and held in memory only, as the welcome's are
(an hour each, 20 at most), until three of its words are typed back with the rotation.

Test: the keyring on disk is the one the phrase unlocked, and the database and a
secret open with the data key it holds.

Verify key (S15.6.5): the 12 words of a copy of the phrase, checked against the keyring
without changing anything, and recorded as a confirmation. A wrong phrase counts toward
the lockout, as at the unlock (S15.4.2).

post.description:
The certificate the peer presented unannounced, accepted once its fingerprint has been
compared with the peer's admin (link-protocol.md §4.5): the password again (S13.7.2).

Create the access key (S11.9.2.1): 12 words, shown once; the password again if given
over 10 minutes ago (S13.7.2).
End a link, or reject a request, or withdraw an invitation.
Pause for a duration, after which it resumes on its own (S11.7.2).
An exchange now rather than at the next hour (S11.7), recorded with who asked (S11.8).

The copy deleted and taken again in full, as a job (S11.9.8, S13.8.7); the password
again if given over 10 minutes ago (S13.7.2).

After a model update: every receipt read again; only empty or suggested fields are
replaced (S9.8.6).

get.description: Sizes and counts only, never what the files hold (S14.10.4).

post.description:
Remove the files no record names, left behind by a restore of an older database under
files written later (S14.6, S16.17). The password again (S13.7.2).

Remove the expired files of the categories ticked, keeping every record; recorded in
Activity with its counts (S14.10.5). No backup first: a backup holds no files, the host's
own backups do.
The answer is the same whether or not the email already has an account (S10.1.4).

get.description: Requests whose email is confirmed, waiting for an admin (S10.1.4).
The starts of statement lines the person asked to ignore (S1.3.3.4), by institution.

post.description: One of them no longer ignored: its lines are read again from the next statement.
A roll proposed for it taken in, or turned down so it isn't offered again (S3.5.3).

get.description: The caller's own tags, by name.

post.description: A filer named by someone else accepts; then the book counts their accounts.

get.description:
The household's people the caller sees, with their relation to the filers on Dec 31
and how the family tree suggests claiming them (S8.14.5.1).
A summary for a preparer: what each panel holds, with its sources.

post.description:
No amendment needed (S8.15): settles the edits made since the federal return was filed,
with who said so and when.
Bulk categorise (S12.2.3): Activity says how many, never which amounts.

get.description: How many transactions arrived after the page loaded: the +N new pill (S12.1.3).
One transaction the caller can see: where a new one's Location leads (S13.8.4).

post.description:
Two identical rows on one day, or two a file gave one id: the answer *both real* is
kept (S1.11.5).

get.description:
The caller's budgets counting a transaction, what it counts as in each, and each one's
leave-out (S7.3.5, S12.2.3). The category is the transaction's, the same in every budget.

post.description:
Keep a bitcoin transaction the explorer or node no longer has: its mark is cleared
(S1.6.2.7). Deleting it is the usual delete.

get.description: The pairs proposed for the caller's own accounts, to confirm or reject.

post.description:
Confirmed, the coins arrive with the lots they left with; rejected, the pair isn't
proposed again.

post.description:
An admin's reset, the last resort when the app and the recovery codes are lost
(S10.1.6): two-step is off, and the user's sessions end. An action, the password given
again.
The welcome's last step: the first admin, signed in at once (S10.1.2).

Three of the words typed back make the key: the keyring is written and the server
unlocks with it (S15.4.4).
A new master key's phrase, held in memory only, until its words are typed back.
